FOR campaign/census-tail -- SECOND RUN: NO GOLDENS MOVED. rc=0 in 1249 s. That is the clean answer for a worldgen change and it is the one that mattered: "reuse fixed capacity tolerances across eras" is byte-identical on your tree. A perf change to code executed 1000 times per census that moves nothing is the good outcome, and it means the delivery caveat I gave you never fires — there is nothing to deliver and nothing to revert.

THE PERF PICTURE, ACROSS ALL FOUR RUNS NOW, AND IT IS STILL UNRESOLVED:

                     total  studies    tail  tail ratio
    the-lot A       1278.2    970.2   307.9        7.36
    the-lot B       1186.0    964.9   221.2        4.46
    yours #1        1197.5    949.9   247.6        4.27
    yours #2        1235.4    951.5   283.9        5.43

    tail across 4 runs: min 221.2, max 307.9, range 86.8 s

Four readings, and the tail still spans 87 s with no trend. Neither of your changes is distinguishable from noise at this resolution. Your #2 tail is HIGHER than your #1, which says nothing either — that is the instrument, not your code.

ONE THING THE FOUR READINGS DO SHOW, and it is not what either of us would have guessed. Your STUDIES come in ~15 s below the-lot's: 949.9 and 951.5 against 970.2 and 964.9. But that gap is present in your run #1, WHICH DOES NOT CONTAIN THE WORLDGEN CHANGE — #1 touched only regenerate-artifacts.sh, which cannot affect study time. So the studies difference is a property of your TREE (you are 194 behind, so it is main's 4 worldgen and 9 lab commits you lack, or box drift), not of your capacity-tolerance work. And between #1 and #2, adding the worldgen change moved studies from 949.9 to 951.5 — up, not down, well inside noise.

So on the evidence available: your worldgen change is SAFE (byte-identical) and has no measurable effect on study time. That is two-thirds of what you want to know and the instrument cannot supply the third.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY RESOLVE IT: not more census runs. Four have now been spent and the noise floor has not moved. The census wraps exactly three timed segments, so both the tail and any within-study effect are only visible by differencing totals against an 87 s spread. Instrumenting the segments — the 747 SVG renders, the domesday survey, the anomaly report, and inside the studies if you want per-phase worldgen numbers — would make a 15 s effect legible where it currently cannot be. That is one run's worth of work and it is the thing standing between everyone and a measurable answer.

Byte-identity is proven; the speed claim is not, in either direction. Worth saying that way round in the ledger.
